provisions.title: Definitions
provisions.description: AI System, Provider, Deployer, Importer, Distributor definitions

provisions.title: Prohibited AI Practices
provisions.description: Ban on manipulative AI, social scoring, biometric categorisation

provisions.title: AI Literacy
provisions.description: Obligation to develop AI literacy measures (as amended by Digital Omnibus)

implications_for_smes: Ban on manipulative AI, social scoring, biometric categorisation (with limited exceptions)
Obligation to develop AI literacy measures for personnel using AI systems
Definition of what constitutes an AI system determines scope of all other obligations

provisions.title: GPAI Provider Obligations
provisions.description: Technical documentation, copyright compliance, incident reporting

implications_for_smes: If your company provides foundation models (GPAI), full compliance required
Most SMEs are deployers not providers of GPAI
Voluntary Codes of Practice available for demonstrating adequacy

provisions.title: Transparency Obligations for Certain AI Systems
provisions.description: Disclosure requirements for chatbots, deepfakes, emotion recognition

provisions.title: Obligations of Deployers
provisions.description: Deployer responsibilities for high-risk AI systems

implications_for_smes: Transparency obligations NOW ACTIVE: Must inform users when interacting with AI
Chatbots must disclose they are AI systems
Deepfakes must be labeled as artificially generated/manipulated
Emotion recognition systems must inform affected persons
National authorities can now impose sanctions
Fines up to EUR 15M or 3% global turnover for prohibited practices
Fines up to EUR 7.5M or 1% for transparency violations
immediate_actions: Review Art. 5 prohibited practices - ensure no banned AI uses
Audit all customer-facing AI for Art. 50 transparency compliance
Label all AI-generated content and deepfakes
Disclose AI use in chatbots and direct interactions
Classify each system: Prohibited / High-Risk / Transparency / Minimal Risk
Implement Art. 4 AI literacy training for relevant staff
Review GDPR compliance for any personal data processing via AI

provisions.title: High-Risk AI Systems (Standalone)
provisions.description: Classification of high-risk AI systems in specified domains

provisions.title: High-Risk Classification
provisions.description: Classification rules for Annex III systems

provisions.title: Full High-Risk Requirements
provisions.description: Risk management, data governance, documentation, logging, oversight, accuracy

affected_domains: Biometrics (remote identification, emotion recognition in workplace/education)
Critical Infrastructure (road traffic, energy, water, digital infrastructure)
Employment & Worker Management (recruitment, promotion, termination, task allocation)
Access to Essential Services (credit scoring, insurance, social benefits)
Justice & Democratic Processes (court evidence, voting, public opinion analysis)
preparation_required: Inventory all AI systems used in these domains
Prepare technical documentation per Annex IV

provisions.title: AI Systems Integrated in Regulated Products
provisions.description: High-risk AI as safety component of regulated products

provisions.title: Product Safety Component Rule
provisions.description: AI systems that are safety components of products under sectoral legislation

special_considerations: These systems must comply with AI Act requirements AND existing product safety regulations
Coordination between AI Act conformity assessment and product certification required

modifications.before: Specific sufficient level of AI literacy required
modifications.after: Simplified obligation - promote AI literacy appropriate to context
modifications.effect: More flexibility, but still mandatory for personnel using AI
Additional 16 months for standalone high-risk systems preparation
Additional 12 months for product-integrated AI systems

modifications.change: Enhanced AI Office powers at EU level with coordinated enforcement approach across Member States
